programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo travels to Uttoxeter from Liverpool, beginning by learning about the design of the city's Metropolitan Cathedral of Christ the King, inaugurated in 1967. At Jodrell Bank, Michael hears how physicist Bernard Lovell's revolutionary research into meteors led to the construction of one of the biggest radio telescopes in the world

programme.title: Walking with Jim Moir
programme.desc: The comedian better known to some as Vic Reeves explores a fascinating corner of the Kent coast as he walks down to Dungeness. Along the way he meets locals, explores military ruins and rides a steam train

programme.title: The Treasures of Ancient Rome
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the artistic achievements of the Romans, tracing their progression from thieves and copycats to pioneers of the use of unflinching realism. Portraits from the Republic reveal how they captured lifelike images and immortalised figures such as Julius Caesar and Cicero using marble, bronze and paint. Alastair also looks at how Rome's first emperor, Augustus, used art as a tool to forge his dominion

programme.title: Caligula with Mary Beard
programme.desc: Roman emperor Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus - better known as Caligula - was said to have made his horse a consul, proclaimed himself a living God and indulged in scandalous orgies. In this documentary, classical scholar Mary Beard attempts to peel away some of the myths surrounding him, sifting through surviving evidence to paint a portrait of the real Caligula

programme.title: Sir Derek Jacobi Remembers - I, Claudius
programme.desc: The veteran actor looks back at the landmark 1976 drama, based on the novels of Robert Graves, telling the life story of a reluctant Roman emperor

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Acclaimed drama set amidst a web of power, corruption and lies, chronicling the reigns of the Roman emperors - Augustus, Tiberius, Caligula and finally Claudius - focusing on the intrigue that surrounded their respective reigns. Augustus's wife Livia schemes to ensure her son Tiberius succeeds her husband. The dispute between Marcus Agrippa and Marcellus reaches boiling point, prompting the former to leave Rome for the East. With Derek Jacobi, Sian Phillips, Brian Blessed and George Baker

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Augustus refuses to forgive Tiberius, but remains blissfully unaware of Julia's philandering. Lucius is promoted to command the army in Spain following the inexplicable death of his brother

programme.desc: From the 2026 Proms, Ryan Wigglesworth conducts the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra, who take to the stage for Elgar's First Symphony. Also, a delve into the archives to look back to Sheku Kanneh-Mason's Cello Concerto performance. Petroc Trelawny presents from the Royal Albert Hall

programme.title: TOTP: 2000
programme.desc: Gail Porter presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on February 25, 2000. Featuring Shania Twain, Jay-Z, Rebecca Wheatley, Eels, CRW, Aqua, Christina Aguilera and All Saints

programme.title: TOTP: 2000
programme.desc: Jamie Theakston presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on March 3, 2000. Featuring Tom Jones & Stereophonics, Daphne & Celeste, A1, Jamelia, The Bluetones, Kelis, Artful Dodger feat Romina Johnson and All Saints

programme.title: TOTP: 1977
programme.desc: Noel Edmonds looks at the weekly pop chart from 1977 and introduces music by the Steve Gibbons Band, the Detroit Emeralds, Boney M, Showaddywaddy, Jonathan Richman and the Modern Lovers, Bob Marley and the Wailers, Dana, Emerson Lake and Palmer, Rita Coolidge, Thin Lizzy and Donna Summer

programme.title: TOTP: 1983
programme.desc: Mike Read and Janice Long introduce an edition of the show from July 28, featuring performances by KC and the Sunshine Band, Elvis Costello and the Attractions, the Lotus Eaters, Malcolm McLaren, Robert Plant and Bananarama

programme.title: Louis Armstrong in Concert
programme.desc: A concert by Louis Armstrong and his All Stars from their 1968 British tour. Songs include Blueberry Hill, Mack the Knife and Wonderful World. The programme was first shown in August 2001 to mark the centenary of the legendary jazz trumpeter and vocalist's birth

programme.title: Louis Armstrong - Show of the Week
programme.desc: Humphrey Lyttelton introduces the legendary jazz trumpeter and singer as he performs alongside the All-Stars during their British visit of 1968. Songs include Blueberry Hill, Mack the Knife, Wonderful World, Hello Dolly and Bare Necessities

programme.title: Jazz Legends in Their Own Words
programme.desc: A journey into the BBC archives, unearthing performances and candid interviews from the golden age of jazz. Featuring some of the greatest names in American music, from Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington and Count Basie to Oscar Peterson, Dizzy Gillespie and Ella Fitzgerald

programme.title: The Fairytale Castles of King Ludwig II with Dan Cruickshank
programme.desc: Documentary exploring the aesthetic styles associated with Ludwig II of Bavaria, the king who was considered to be handsome and loved by his people. Dan Cruickshank investigates the mock-medievalism of Neuschwanstein castle and the complex design of Herrenchiemsee, to assess how they are key to learning more about the enigmatic ruler

programme.title: Cairngorms: A Year in the Wild
programme.desc: A tour of Britain's largest national park, a land of extremes in the heart of the Highlands, where a diverse range of wildlife including golden eagles, ptarmigan, capercaillie, red deer and crested tits can be found. The programme explores the area through the eyes of people who live and work there, including a mountain guide, an artist, a gamekeeper and a nature writer. Narrated by Hermione Norris

programme.title: Great Violinists at the Proms
programme.desc: Katie Derham presents a look at some of the great performances on the violin that have graced the Royal Albert Hall stage. Rising star Sueye Park makes her Proms debut with the Sibelius Violin Concerto, also featuring archive gems from Liya Petrova, Nicola Benedetti and Nigel Kennedy

programme.title: Bill Paterson Remembers - The Cheviot, The Stag and The Black, Black Oil
programme.desc: Actor Bill Paterson looks back on one of the earliest roles of his career, in the 1974 boundary-breaking television adaptation of John McGrath's play The Cheviot, The Stag and The Black, Black Oil, which featured outdoor historical re-enactments of the notorious Highland Clearances intercut with scenes from a live performance of the play. Bill's involvement with the production began when he was a young member of the left wing theatre company '7:84' - so named to reflect their claim that seven percent of the population owned 84 percent of the UK's wealth - and saw him originally playing not one but two roles, as Glasgow property speculator McChuckemup and the oilman known as 'Texas Bill'

programme.title: The Cheviot, the Stag and the Black, Black Oil
programme.desc: A 1974 drama documentary adaptation of John McGrath's play staged by the 7:84 theatre company, exploring elements of Scottish history. Starring Bill Paterson and Dolina MacLennan

programme.title: 7:84 : Keep Right On? - Ex-S
programme.desc: Robert Dawson Scott presents an in-depth look at fortunes of the 7:84 Theatre Company, founded by John McGrath in late 1960s. Including excerpts from stage performances and archive interviews. First broadcast in 1993

programme.title: Munro: Mountain Man
programme.desc: The story of Victorian adventurer Hugh Munro and his determination to list and climb all the Scottish mountains whose height exceeds 3,000ft. Nicholas Crane visits some of the country's spectacular mountains as he explores the adventurer's bid to reach more than 500 peaks and reveals how his name has been adopted by climbing enthusiasts pursuing the same goal, a pastime known as Munro bagging

programme.title: DR NZ
programme.desc: Dr Euan MacDonald travels to New Zealand to work at Rotorua hospital, alongside one of the highest M?ori populations in the country. Euan meets fellow Gaels who have made New Zealand their home and explores this precious ecosystem of geothermal activity. Euan faces hard decisions - he breaks devastating news and deals with patients discharging against medical advice. He sees the hospital's M?ori dedicated healthcare team in action, learns some Te Reo M?ori and experiences how M?ori culture is reflected within the hospital

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: On Papa Westray, Paul's visiting nephews are roped into farm work, while Paul and Mel have lots to do for their long-awaited wedding day. It's a concerning time for Sally as some of her ewes are struck down by a devastating mystery illness. In Fife, Andy and Jo increase their loan to install another holiday pod and take 400 lambs to market to raise some much-needed cash

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson work on the garden's borders, replanting, filling gaps and replacing losses all around the plot. Kirsty will also be planting in the border behind Beechgrove's main pond, where other gaps have appeared, and she is building a new structure to create a habitat for pollinators

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Ayr, crewmates Sophie and Shelby are called to a critical incident in which Irene has suffered a burst gastric ulcer and is losing pints of blood. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based paramedic Andrew, technician Simon and student Matthew treat Patrick, who is displaying a range of worrying symptoms, including a worsening headache, a rash and a sensitivity to light. The team can't rule out meningitis, but encounter a queue of ambulances outside Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven

programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year 2024
programme.desc: Judges Anna Campbell-Jones, Banjo Beale and Danny Campbell visit properties in central Scotland. The first home for the judges to visit is the Old Mill near Dunblane, an empty industrial building converted a five-bedroom home. Next up is Sandstone Villa in Bridge of Allan, a semi-deteched property which dates back to the early 1900s. Finally, the judges visit Courtyard Farmhouse, a conversion of a once-derelict farmhouse between Falkirk and Linlithgow

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: Area operations manager Fiona Galbraith travels to Stornoway from her home on Benbecula to help out with a freight backlog and keep the essential supply lines open between the mainland and the Outer Hebrides. Sisters Natalie and Tanya Mackay from the Isle of Lewis are now a couple of weeks into their modern apprenticeship with CalMac and are about to join a vessel for the first time

programme.title: Mhairi Black: Being Me Again
programme.desc: The ex-SNP MP talks about her life in depth. As well as interviews with her wife Katie, and father Alan, cameras gain access at the House of Commons, and the first night of her stand-up show, Politics Isn't for Me, at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. Mhairi, the youngest person elected to the House of Commons, also discusses feelings about her own neurodivergence

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: Roisin is at her wits end when she reaches breaking point over Gillian's behaviour and Jodie drops a bombshell. Chris is forced to face the music when he realises paying Nicole is impossible, Tyler struggles to get dirt on Alex, and Amber considers her next steps with Angus

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: After accidentally picking up one of Cathy's novels, Agnes discovers she has a surprising fondness for steamy fiction. She then gatecrashes the next group meeting of Cathy's book group to share her insights on the genre, - mortifying her daughter in the process. Comedy, co-written by and starring Brendan O'Carroll, with Jennifer Gibney

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: The criminologist explores how if a killer wants to get away with murder, they must get rid of the evidence - in other words, their victim - and their attempts to do that

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Glasgow, Paul and Ryan of the Special Operations Response Team are called to a siege in a flat, where a man has barricaded himself inside and is threatening to harm himself. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based crewmates Kirsty and Bruce are called to see Rebecca, who has suffered a severe anaphylactic attack, but she shows little sign of improvement after several doses of adrenaline, prompting a rapid journey on blue-lights to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

programme.title: Rikki

This film tells the story of his extraordinary life by bringing together the people closest to him and the people he inspired, with never-before-seen home movie footage and clips of the best-loved moments of his career

programme.title: Still Game

programme.title: Rip It Up

Contributors include Jim Kerr, Alan Rankine, Emma Pollock Martin Bulloch, Stuart Braithwaite, Dougie Vipond, Ricky Ross, Charlie and Craig Reid, Sharleen Spiteri , KT Tunstall, Duglas Stewart, Sean Dickson and Alan McGee

To succeed he must befriend the animals, learn as much as he can about them, and try to win their trust and respect, discovering how these creatures have evolved in the most unusual ways to survive and prosper in one of the most hostile environments on the planet

programme.desc: Steve Backshall presents some of his favourite moments from the wildlife series, including abseiling into the Gomantong cave system and meeting a hippo

programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May try to make train travel cheaper, faster and more interesting, replacing the locomotive with a specially modified car and the carriages with a series of caravans. Comedy star Rowan Atkinson gets behind the wheel of the Reasonably Priced Car and Jeremy drives the Jaguar XKR-S and a Nissan GT-R round the track to compare both models

programme.title: I Am Legend
programme.desc: A Manhattan-based military scientist finds himself immune to a virus that turns humans into ferocious vampire-like creatures. Sci-fi thriller, starring Will Smith, Alice Braga and Charlie Tahan

programme.desc: Part one of two. The story of Alex Batty, who went missing when he was 11 on what was supposed to be a short family holiday with his mother and grandfather. programme.desc: The reporter follows a group of Ukrainian civilians as they arrive in the UK for five weeks of intensive army training before deployment to the frontline fighting against Russia. Among the group is florist and gardener Mykola who wants to join his family members on the frontline and fight towards victory so he can marry his girlfriend. For Pasha, a welder who was living abroad when the invasion began, he fears going into battle means never seeing his parents again

programme.title: Roman Kemp: The Fight for Young Lives
programme.desc: Broadcaster Roman Kemp knows first-hand the impact of serious mental health issues. In 2020, he made Our Silent Emergency in the wake of the death of a friend. programme.title: The Hundred Live
programme.desc: MI London Women v Manchester Super Giants Women (Start-time 2.30pm). Coverage of the match from Kia Oval. Beth Mooney put in a player of the match performance for the Manchester franchise last season, when they were known as the Originals and served as hosts against the team formerly known as Oval Invincibles. Mooney's knock of 70 off 45 balls propelled her side to a first innings total of 139/6, which the Invincibles fell just short of in their run chase as they were held to 137/3

programme.title: The Hundred Live
programme.desc: MI London Men v Manchester Super Giants Men (Start-time 6.00pm). Coverage of the match from Kia Oval in London. These two teams met last year at this ground with the game ending in a resounding nine-wicket victory for the London team. The Super Giants, known as the Originals last year, were bowled out for just 128 before the hosts reached their target with a massive 43 balls to spare, as Will Jacks hit 61 from just 26 balls

programme.desc: The Washington DC Open. Coverage of day two of the WTA 500 and ATP 500 event, a hard-court tournament held at William H.G. FitzGerald Tennis Center in the USA. Americans McCartney Kessler and Caroline Dolehide were involved in the only match to require a third set in the opening round of the women's draw last year, and it was the latter who prevailed 7-6 5-7 6-3. Emma Raducanu and Katie Boulter were the only British entrants and experienced contrasting fortunes, with Raducanu booking her place in round two with 7-6 6-4 win over Marta Kostyuk, while Boulter suffered an early exit after losing 3-6 4-6 to Maria Sakkari

programme.desc: The Washington DC Open. Coverage of day three of the WTA 500 and ATP 500 event, a hard-court tournament held at William H.G. FitzGerald Tennis Center in the USA. All three of the British players involved in the second round of last year's competition emerged victorious, with Emma Raducanu beating four-time Grand slam champion Naomi Osaka in straight sets, while Dan Evans triumphed 6-4 6-4 over Alex Michelsen, and Cameron Norrie beat the number two seed Lorenzo Musetti 3-6 6-2 6-3. Perhaps the most notable victory was claimed by 2021 US Open runner-up Leylah Fernandez, who eliminated the number one seed Jessica Pegula in a see-saw encounter that finished 6-3 1-6 7-5 in her favour
